title: Shopping
subtitle: ဈေးဝယ်ခြင်း

categories.desc: Looking around, and asking for what you want.
cards: I'm just looking, thanks.
The polite answer when a shop assistant asks Can I help you? and you don't need help yet.
— Can I help you? — I'm just looking, thanks.
Do you have this in blue?
Asks for another colour or size of the same thing.
I like this shirt. Do you have it in green?
ဒီရှပ်အင်္ကျီ ကြိုက်တယ်။ အစိမ်းရောင် ရှိလား။
Where can I find rice?
ဆန် ဘယ်မှာ ရှိလဲ။
In a big shop or supermarket.
Excuse me, where can I find the eggs?
တဆိတ်လောက်၊ ကြက်ဥ ဘယ်မှာ ရှိလဲ။
Do you sell batteries?
When you aren't sure the shop has it at all.
Do you sell phone chargers?
Can I try it on?
ဝတ်ကြည့်လို့ ရမလား။
For clothes and shoes. Try on = put on to see if it fits.
I like these trousers. Can I try them on?
ဒီဘောင်းဘီ ကြိုက်တယ်။ ဝတ်ကြည့်လို့ ရမလား။

categories.desc: Asking how much, and talking about the price.
cards: How much is this?
ဒါ ဘယ်လောက်လဲ။
For one thing. Point to it as you ask.
Excuse me, how much is this bag?
တဆိတ်လောက်၊ ဒီအိတ် ဘယ်လောက်လဲ။
How much are these?
ဒါတွေ ဘယ်လောက်လဲ။
For more than one thing: these, those, the apples.
How much are the mangoes?
သရက်သီးတွေ ဘယ်လောက်လဲ။
That's too expensive.
Polite enough, but softer: It's a bit expensive for me.
Ten thousand? That's too expensive.
Is there a discount?
Asks if the price is lower today, or for students, or for buying two.
Is there a discount if I buy three?
Can you give me a better price?
Bargaining, as in a market. In shops in Britain or America, prices are usually fixed.
It's nice, but can you give me a better price?
Do you have a smaller size?
Or a bigger size, a larger size.
These shoes are too big. Do you have a smaller size?
ဒီဖိနပ်က ကြီးလွန်းတယ်။ ဆိုဒ် အသေး ရှိလား။
It's too big.
Too + adjective: too small, too long, too tight.
The jacket is too big for me.
ဂျာကင်က ကျွန်မအတွက် ကြီးလွန်းတယ်။
It fits perfectly.
အတိအကျ တော်တယ်။
Fit is about size. Suit is about style or colour.
I'll buy this dress. It fits perfectly.
ဒီဝတ်စုံ ဝယ်မယ်။ အတိအကျ တော်တယ်။
I'll take it.
ဒါ ယူမယ်။
You've decided to buy it. For more than one: I'll take them.
OK, I'll take it. And this one too.
အိုကေ၊ ဒါ ယူမယ်။ ဒါလည်း ယူမယ်။
I'll leave it, thanks.
A polite way to say you won't buy it.
Hmm, I'll leave it, thanks. Maybe next time.
အင်း၊ မယူတော့ဘူး၊ ကျေးဇူးပါ။ နောက်မှ ဝယ်မယ်။

categories.desc: At the till: card or cash, a bag, the receipt.
cards: Do you take cards?
Asks if you can pay by card. Also: Can I pay by card?
Do you take cards, or only cash?
ကတ်နဲ့ ပေးလို့ ရလား၊ ဒါမှမဟုတ် ငွေသားပဲလား။
Can I pay in cash?
In cash, by card. Or with a phone: Can I pay with KBZPay?
Can I pay in cash? I don't have a card.
Can I have a bag, please?
အိတ် တစ်လုံး ရနိုင်မလား။
Some shops charge for bags or don't give them unless you ask.
Can I have a bag, please? I have a lot of things.
အိတ် တစ်လုံး ရနိုင်မလား။ ပစ္စည်း အများကြီး ပါလို့။
Can I have the receipt?
ဘောက်ချာ ရနိုင်မလား။
Keep the receipt if you might bring something back.
Can I have the receipt, please?
ဘောက်ချာ ရနိုင်မလား။
Keep the change.
You don't want the extra money back. Common with taxi drivers.
Here's ten dollars. Keep the change.
ဒေါ်လာ ဆယ် ပါ။ အကြွေ ယူထားလိုက်ပါ။

categories.my: ဆိုင်ဝန်ထမ်း ပြောတတ်တာများ
categories.desc: Phrases you will hear at the till, so you can answer.
cards: Anything else?
Answer: No, that's all, thanks. Or name the next thing.
— Anything else? — No, that's all, thanks.
That's five thousand kyats.
ငါးထောင်ကျပ် ကျပါတယ်။
Tells you the total. Also: That'll be five thousand kyats.
Two coffees? That's five thousand kyats, please.
ကော်ဖီ နှစ်ခွက်လား။ ငါးထောင်ကျပ် ကျပါတယ်။
Cash or card?
Asks how you want to pay. Answer: Cash, please. / Card, please.
— Cash or card? — Card, please.
Would you like a bag?
အိတ် ယူမလား။
Answer: Yes, please. / No, thanks, I have one.
— Would you like a bag? — No, thanks. I have one.
Here's your change.
ပြန်အမ်းငွေ ပါ။
The money you get back. Count it and say Thank you.
Here's your change, and your receipt.
ပြန်အမ်းငွေနဲ့ ဘောက်ချာ ပါ။
